nodes.body: The sun was warm and the sand was warm, and the sea had gone away for a while. It was low tide, Milo's favorite morning of all, when the water pulls back and leaves its secrets behind on the rocks. Gran wore her big beach hat and carried the picnic basket on one arm. Milo swung his red bucket, clank, clank, as they walked. Ahead, the wet rocks sparkled with tide pools, dozens of little mirrors catching the sun. "The sea always comes back," Gran said, "just like a friend coming home." Milo grinned. He could not wait to explore the low-tide rocks and pools.

choices.label: Follow Gran down the sandy path.

nodes.body: Gran led the way down the sandy path and spread her towel on her flat rock, the spot where she could see the whole beach at once. "Remember the rules," she said, tucking a strand of hair under her hat. "Stay on the dry rocks. Wet feet are perfectly fine. And call if you ever want a hand." Milo saluted like a sailor. "Yes, Gran!" Then he turned toward the shining pools, already humming with excitement, and stepped off the sand and onto the rocks.

choices.label: Step out onto the flat low-tide rocks.

nodes.body: Out on the rocks, Milo heard tiny voices calling. Low tide had left some tide-pool friends stranded, too high and dry: a sea star stuck on a bare ledge, a fish trapped in a shrinking puddle, a crab tangled in seaweed, and a periwinkle marooned on a sunny rock. Far off, the sparkling sea was already turning around to come home, and it would reach the rocks again before long. Everyone was calling at once, and Milo could only reach one friend at a time. Who should he help first?

choices.label: Hurry to the sea star on the high ledge.
Follow a flappy splashing sound across the rocks.
Follow a busy clack-clack-clack sound to the seaweed patch.
Climb toward something tiny gleaming in the sunshine on the dry rock.

nodes.body: Milo reached the tall rock where Stella the sea star sat stranded on her bare high ledge, high above his head. Her five arms drooped like a tired star sticker peeling off a page. "Down here!" Milo called, and Stella lifted one weary arm to wave. "The ledge is getting warm," she said in a small, patient voice, "and I would very much like to be back in my deep cool pool."

choices.label: Climb the low steps for a closer look.

nodes.body: Milo climbed two safe, flat steps for a closer look. Stella perked up, waving with one arm like a tiny periscope. The ledge was dry as toast, and her deep cool pool waited just below, glinting invitingly. "Any rescue plan is fine with me," Stella said. "I am a very patient sea star." Milo looked at his red bucket, then at his own two hands, then at the little slope between them, and began to think hard.

choices.label: Think up a rescue plan for Stella.

nodes.body: Milo lined up his ideas while Stella waved cheerfully from her dry ledge. He could toss water up to her with his cupped hands, or carry his bucket up the little slope to pour her a waterfall, or simply wet his hands and slide her gently down himself. Over on her flat rock, Gran watched and waited, ready with a tip the moment he wanted one. Milo rubbed his chin. Which plan should he try?

choices.label: Toss water up with your cupped hands.
Carry his red bucket up the little slope.
Wet your hands and gently slide Stella down.

nodes.body: Milo scooped seawater into his cupped hands and tossed it up toward the ledge. Splash, splish, plip, plop, it rained straight back down onto his own head! Stella giggled so hard her arms wiggled like ribbons in the wind. Milo laughed too and shook his wet hair like a puppy after a bath. No harm done, just a soggy fringe. He could line up his plans again, or trot over and ask Gran for a tip.

choices.label: Line up the plans and try again.
Ask Gran for a tip.

nodes.body: Milo filled his red bucket at the nearest pool and started up the little slope, but the bucket wobbled, tipped, and whooshed every last drop over his own shoes. Squelch, squelch went his toes. Stella clapped two arms together for the marvelous splash. Milo grinned down at his soggy feet; no harm done, and the tide had plenty more water where that came from. He could go back to his plans, or ask Gran for a tip.

choices.label: Shake off the splash and try again.
Ask Gran for a tip.

nodes.body: Gran tipped back her big beach hat and smiled. "Sea stars like things slow and gentle," she said. "Wet your hands first, so Stella can hold on comfortably, then slide her down to her pool, like a little water slide." Milo could try the gentle sliding idea right away, or look over his plans once more.

choices.label: Try Gran's gentle sliding idea.
Look over the plans once more.

nodes.body: Milo dipped his hands into the pool until they were cool and wet, then reached up. Stella held on tight with all five arms. Slow and gentle, he carried her down the rock and into her deep cool pool with a soft, happy ploop. Once she was settled, Stella stretched every arm out wide, like a joyful little dance underwater.

choices.label: Watch Stella settle into her pool.

nodes.body: Stella pressed one arm against the glassy top of the water, like a high five just for Milo, and burbled a bubbly thank you. Back across the rocks, other small voices were still calling, and the tide was coming on. Milo could pick his way out to the pools again, watch the tide arrive, or sit with Gran and let the sea finish the rescuing.

choices.label: Pick your way back out to the pools.
Watch the tide come in over the pools.
Sit with Gran and let the tide finish the rescuing.

nodes.body: Milo hopped carefully from flat rock to flat rock, following a flappy, splashing sound. Out past the pools, the tide had crept one sparkly step closer, glittering as it came. Gran waved her big beach hat from her flat rock. Ahead, the splashing grew louder and louder, coming from a puddle no bigger than a dinner plate.

choices.label: Kneel beside the shrinking puddle.

nodes.body: In the little puddle, a small silver fish zipped in busy circles, round and round. The puddle was only as deep as a soup bowl, and the warm sun was sipping it smaller by the minute. He popped his mouth up above the surface. "My name's Flick," he said, "and I would very much like a bigger pool, please!" He sounded hopeful and chatty, never scared at all.

choices.label: Lean in and say hello to the little fish.

nodes.body: Milo crouched beside the puddle. "Help is here, Flick," he said. "The big deep pool is just two hops away, calm and shady." Flick zoomed an excited lap around his shrinking puddle, sending up little sparkling drops. Milo looked from his own two quick hands, to the strip of sand between the puddles, to his red bucket, weighing three different ways this rescue might go.

choices.label: Think up a plan to move Flick.

nodes.body: Milo studied the puddle while Flick swam hopeful loops around and around. He could try to catch him with his bare hands, or dig a little river through the sand so the puddle could flow to the big deep pool, or dip his bucket and scoop the whole puddle up, fish and all. Flick blew a bubble that seemed to say, you can do it! Milo tapped his chin, thinking it over.

choices.label: Catch Flick with your bare hands.
Dig a little river over to the big deep pool.
Scoop water and Flick up together in his red bucket.

nodes.body: Milo cupped his hands and reached in, but Flick was quicker than a sneeze. He zipped between Milo's fingers, tickled his thumb, and splashed a tiny wave right up Milo's nose! Milo snorted with laughter, and Flick did a proud little flip in celebration. No harm done to anyone, just a wet nose and a giggling fish. Milo could pick a plan again, or ask Gran for a tip.

choices.label: Line up the plans and try again.
Ask Gran for a tip.

nodes.body: Milo dragged his finger through the sand to dig a little river, but the thirsty sand drank the water down with a polite little glug before it could travel anywhere. The channel just sat there, damp and empty. Milo patted the sand and giggled at his own disappearing river. Flick shrugged his fins from the puddle. Milo could pick a plan again, or ask Gran for a tip.

choices.label: Smooth the sand and try again.
Ask Gran for a tip.

nodes.body: Gran leaned forward from her flat rock and smiled. "Fish don't like to be squeezed," she said, "but they do love to swim. Dip your bucket and scoop him up, water and all, and he can ride to the big pool swimming the whole way." Milo could try the gentle scoop, or look over his plans once more.

choices.label: Scoop water and Flick up together, Gran's way.
Look over the plans once more.

nodes.body: Milo lowered his red bucket slowly into the puddle, and Flick swam right in, riding his very own cupful of sea. Two careful hops later, Milo tipped the bucket at the edge of the big deep pool, and Flick poured out with the water in one silvery splash, zooming a giant loop around his cool new home.

choices.label: Watch Flick zoom around his big new pool.

nodes.body: Flick leaped in one sparkling thank-you hop and raced another happy lap around his new pool. Out across the rocks, somebody else was still calling, and the tide was coming on. Milo waved goodbye, grinning, and could head back toward the calling, or stay a moment and watch the water arrive.

choices.label: Head back out toward the calling.
Watch the tide come in over the pools.

nodes.body: Milo crossed the rocks, following a busy clack-clack-clack sound. Behind him, the tide had slid another sparkly step up the sand, filling the farthest pools first, like a row of little cups. Ahead, the seaweed patch was green and glossy in the sun, and something in the middle of it was waving.

choices.label: Cross the rocks to the seaweed patch.

nodes.body: In the seaweed patch, a small crab sat tangled in slippery ribbons, like a present that had wrapped itself. He clacked his claws in a friendly hello. "I'm Pinch," he said. "I was climbing through when the seaweed flopped right over me, and now my legs are in a friendly muddle." He sounded cheerful, not frightened at all, waving one loose claw like a little flag.

choices.label: Crouch down beside the tangled crab.

nodes.body: Milo crouched close, and Pinch wiggled to show which legs were stuck. The seaweed was shiny and slippery as wet noodles. "Don't worry," Pinch said, "my claws only pinch things that poke too fast." Milo looked at the tangle, then at the picnic spoon poking out of his pocket, and began to think hard about the best way to help.

choices.label: Think up a plan to untangle Pinch.

nodes.body: Milo considered the seaweed muddle while Pinch waited, waving his one free claw like a tiny flag. He could give the seaweed one quick tug, or hold out the picnic spoon for Pinch to grab, or untangle one ribbon at a time, nice and slow. Nearby, Gran hummed a beach tune from her flat rock. Milo looked at the tangle from every angle, wondering which plan would work best.

choices.label: Give the seaweed one quick tug.
Hold out the picnic spoon for Pinch to grab.
Untangle one seaweed ribbon at a time.

nodes.body: Milo gripped the slippery seaweed and gave one quick tug. The wet ribbon slid straight through his fingers, and Milo sat down, plop, in a shallow warm puddle! Pinch waved both claws as if to say, whoa, nice splash. Milo laughed and stood up dripping, completely fine, though the tangle was still very much tangled. He could pick a plan again, or ask Gran for a tip.

choices.label: Stand up and try again.
Ask Gran for a tip.

nodes.body: Milo held out the picnic spoon, and Pinch grabbed it, but instead of climbing free, the little crab pinched on tight and waved the spoon around like a shiny trophy. Milo had a gentle, giggly tug-of-war just to get his spoon back, then tucked it safely into his pocket. The tangle was still tangled. He could pick a plan again, or ask Gran for a tip.

choices.label: Pocket the spoon and try again.
Ask Gran for a tip.

nodes.body: Gran called over softly from her flat rock. "Tangles hate hurrying," she said. "Hum a slow song, and untangle one ribbon at a time. The whole knot will give up all by itself." Milo could try the slow, ribbon-by-ribbon way, or look over his plans once more before deciding.

choices.label: Untangle one ribbon at a time, Gran's way.
Look over the plans once more.

nodes.body: Milo hummed a slow beach song and loosened one green ribbon, then another, then another. The tangle gave up at last with a soft slurp, and Pinch stepped free, stretching each leg out one by one, like a tiny gym class. The cool pool beside the seaweed waited, deep and ready, right where he belonged.

choices.label: Watch Pinch scuttle into the cool pool.

nodes.body: Pinch clacked a happy drumroll on a pebble and scuttled a thank-you circle around his pool. Another voice was still calling somewhere back across the rocks, and the tide was coming on. Milo could go and find who was calling, watch the water arrive, or curl up on Gran's towel and let the tide fetch the periwinkle instead.

choices.label: Go and find who is calling.
Watch the tide come in over the pools.
Watch from Gran's her towel while the tide fetches the periwinkle.

nodes.body: Milo tiptoed up the dry rock, following something tiny gleaming in the sunshine, careful to keep his feet on the rough gray parts, the way Gran liked. The tide was closer now, filling pool after pool behind him with happy gurgles. Near the top, a shell no bigger than a button sat all alone in the sun.

choices.label: Tiptoe up the dry rock to the tiny shell.

nodes.body: Near the top of the dry rock sat a periwinkle shell, no bigger than a button, far from any water at all. A tiny voice inside gave a small, polite cough. The sun was warm, the rock was very dry, and the shell was a very long walk from home for someone so small.

choices.label: Bend down and greet the little periwinkle.

nodes.body: Milo bent down, and the tiny shell peeked out. "My name is Winnie," she said. "I went exploring at low tide and wandered much too far." Her cool pool was down the rock, a very long way for a periwinkle, the slowest walkers on the whole beach. Milo dipped one hand into a nearby pool and thought hard about how to help.

choices.label: Think up a plan to bring Winnie home.

nodes.body: Milo thought it over while Winnie waited, snug inside her shell. He could roll her along like a tiny wheel, or cheer her on to walk faster, or offer her a slow, steady ride on his wet palm. "Any way is fine with me," Winnie said. "I am in no hurry at all, though the tide rather is." Milo weighed each idea carefully before choosing.

choices.label: Roll Winnie along like a tiny wheel.
Cheer for Winnie to walk faster.
Offer Winnie a ride on your wet palm.

nodes.body: Milo gave Winnie the gentlest nudge, hoping she would roll like a tiny wheel, but she tucked herself snugly into her shell and simply would not budge, stuck fast as a pebble glued to the rock. "No rolling today, thank you," came a tiny muffled voice. Milo laughed at his own fizzled idea, and Winnie peeked back out, perfectly comfy. He could pick a plan again, or ask Gran for a tip.

choices.label: Smile at the stubborn shell and try again.
Ask Gran for a tip.

nodes.body: Milo clapped and cheered, "Go, Winnie, go!" Winnie tried her very fastest, and after one whole minute of mighty effort, she had traveled the width of a single pebble. She puffed proudly. At this speed, they might arrive by next Tuesday! Milo cheered once more anyway, because trying always deserves a cheer. He could pick a plan again, or ask Gran for a tip.

choices.label: Line up the plans and try again.
Ask Gran for a tip.

nodes.body: Gran cupped her hands around her mouth and called up gently. "Little periwinkles ride better than they roll," she said. "Wet your palm so it feels like home, let Winnie hold on tight, and walk her down slow as a Sunday." Milo could offer the wet-palm ride, or look over his plans once more.

choices.label: Offer Winnie a wet-palm ride, Gran's way.
Look over the plans once more.

nodes.body: Milo wet his palm in a pool and laid his hand flat beside Winnie. She slid aboard and held on snug. This was the longest, highest, most careful rescue of the whole day, step by slow step down the big rock, while the tide gurgled behind him like a cheering crowd, until at last he knelt at the edge of her cool pool.

choices.label: Lower Winnie into her cool pool.

nodes.body: Winnie settled onto her favorite green stone with a tiny, happy squeak, home at last. A bright gurgle ran all along the rocks as the tide came on. Milo could look back across the rocks for anyone else still calling, or stay right there and watch the water arrive.

choices.label: Look back across the rocks for anyone else.
Watch the tide come in over the pools.

nodes.body: Milo stood tall on the flat rocks and looked back over all the pools he had reached. Every friend he had helped was safe and settled, waving, drumming, or zooming happily in the water. The tide swept closer in sparkly stripes, warm and friendly, coming to welcome everyone home and finish what Milo had started. From her flat rock, Gran gave Milo a proud thumbs up, her hat tipped back in the sun.

choices.label: Watch the first wave-finger slide in.

nodes.body: The first thin finger of the tide slid across the rocks and filled the nearest pool right up to its brim. The water was home, and it was reaching every pool Milo could not get to as well. The pools fizzed and sparkled like a celebration. Milo could follow the tide from pool to pool to watch each friend greet it, climb up beside Gran on her flat rock to watch it all at once, or open the picnic basket to celebrate the rescue team.

choices.label: Follow the tide from pool to pool.
Climb up beside Gran on Gran's flat rock.
Open the picnic basket to celebrate.

nodes.body: Milo trotted beside the tide as it filled pool after pool, like a row of teacups being poured one by one. Stella's pool was next, already trembling at the brim. Milo could stay and cheer as her pool spilled over, race the soft foam line up the dry sand just for fun, or peek around for anyone else who might still need a hand.

choices.label: Cheer as Stella's pool spills over.
Race the foam line up the dry sand.
Peek around for anyone else who needs help.

nodes.body: Milo lined up his toes on the dry sand, well ahead of the water, and waited for the soft foam line to catch up. "Ready, steady, go!" Gran called from her flat rock. The tide whooshed gently forward, and Milo took off giggling, racing along the dry sand right beside it.

choices.label: Run the last few splashy-sounding steps.

nodes.body: Milo shaded his eyes and looked over the busy, filling pools. Nobody was calling for help anymore, but under a shadowy ledge, something small bobbed on the new water, and along the wet sand, a glittery trail wound toward a heap of shining pebbles. Both looked like tiny mysteries worth one last look before the picnic basket.

choices.label: Peek under the shadowy ledge.
Follow the glittery trail.

nodes.body: Milo climbed up beside Gran on her flat rock, and she wrapped him in the warm corner of her towel. Below them, the tide filled every pool one by one while the friends waved, splashed, and clacked happily. "How should the rescue team celebrate?" Gran asked. They could sing a welcome-home song, shout three hip-hip-hoorays, or call each friend by name as their pool filled up.

choices.label: Sing the welcome-home song.
Shout three hip-hip-hoorays.
Call each friend's name as their pool fills.

nodes.body: Gran opened the picnic basket on her flat rock: crackers, berries, and two little cups of juice. Below them, the tide sparkled into the last pools while the friends splashed a happy hello to it. Milo could raise his juice cup in a toast to the rescue team, tell Gran the whole story of the rescue day, or start planning the next low-tide rescue patrol.

choices.label: Raise juice cups to the rescue team.
Tell Gran the whole rescue story.
Plan the next low tide rescue patrol.

nodes.body: Milo snuggled next to Gran on her towel and shared crackers while the tide slid in. The water reached Flick, and his puddle grew into a lake; it unwrapped Pinch from his seaweed and carried Winnie gently home, doing the rest of the rescuing all by itself. Milo waved to each friend as they floated free and happy. "One rescue by you, and three by the tide," Gran said. "What a fine team." Milo snuggled deeper into the warm towel, proud of Stella's rescue, already excited to come back and visit the brimming pools.

From Gran's towel, Milo watched the sparkly tide climb the rock, higher and higher, until it reached tiny Winnie's shell and lifted her like a leaf on a stream. The little periwinkle sailed down to her pool in style, and a tiny, faraway wheee floated across the rocks. "Three rescues by you, and one by the tide," Gran said. "Sounds like a fine team to me." Milo waved and waved until the little shell settled safely into her deep, cool water.

The tide tipped over the rim of Stella's pool, and the water rose around her like a big, cool hug. Stella did a slow, magnificent underwater cartwheel of thank you, all five arms sparkling in the sun. Milo cheered, Gran cheered from her flat rock, and the tide kept rolling gently in, welcoming every rescued friend home. "Best low tide ever," Milo decided, watching the pools fizz and glitter, and Stella cartwheeled once more, as if she completely agreed.

Milo and the foam line raced up the beach, and Milo won by exactly one giggling toe. The tide pit-pattered little wave-claps behind him and filled the last pools while Gran shouted hooray from her flat rock. Milo took a big bow toward the tide, and it seemed to bow back with one soft, sparkly wave. Every friend was home, the water was back where it belonged, and Milo was, without a doubt, the fastest rescuer on the whole beach.

Under the shadowy ledge bobbed a hermit crab in a curly, borrowed shell, already floating home on the new water and needing no rescue at all. He tipped his shell to Milo, exactly the way Gran tipped her big beach hat. Milo tipped an invisible hat right back, grinning. A new friend to wave to, as the tide carried him gently past the rocks, while all the rescued friends settled happily into their brimming pools.

The glittery trail wound between two pebbles and stopped at a perfect shell, striped like a peppermint, polished smooth by the tide. "A thank-you gift from the beach," Gran said, "for a hard-working rescuer." Milo held it to his ear and heard the tide inside, whooshing softly home. He carried it back in his red bucket, a treasure to remember this whole rescue day forever.

Milo and Gran made up a welcome-home song right there on her flat rock, with a happy sound for Stella, for Flick, for Pinch, and for Winnie. The friends joined in from their brimming pools, splashing along in time, while the tide kept the beat with soft, steady whooshes. The song floated out over the sparkling water until every single pool was full and every single friend was home at last.

"Hip hip hooray! Hip hip hooray! Hip hip hooray!" Milo and Gran shouted three big cheers as the tide rolled home across the rocks, and the friends answered back with splashes, bubbles, and happy claw-clacks from their pools. The tide filled the very last pool with one happy gulp. Every friend was safe, every pool was brimming, and the whole beach felt like it was clapping right along with them.

As each pool filled, Milo called its friend by name. "Welcome home, Stella. Welcome home, Flick. Welcome home, Pinch. Welcome home, Winnie." Each friend popped up and waved an arm, or a fin, or a claw, or a tiny shell, then settled snug into the deep cool water. Gran squeezed Milo's shoulder, smiling. Every single friend was home again, safe and happy, and Milo was the reason why.

Milo and Gran clinked their little juice cups together on her flat rock. "To the rescue team," Gran said, "to Stella, Flick, Pinch, and Winnie, and to the helper who never gave up." Below them, the tide sparkled into every pool while the friends splashed a fizzy toast of their own. Milo sipped his juice slowly, watching the whole shining beach settle into place, and decided that rescue days tasted especially sweet.

ending.title: A Toast to the Rescue Team

nodes.body: Milo told Gran the whole story of the rescue day: Stella stranded on her bare high ledge, Flick trapped in his shrinking puddle, Pinch tangled up in slippery seaweed, and the long, slow ride home for the littlest shell of all. Gran listened under her big beach hat and declared it the best beach story she had ever heard. Below them, the full pools sparkled and the friends splashed, as if adding in their own favorite parts of the tale.

Milo and Gran planned the next low-tide rescue patrol, drawing cracker-crumb maps on her towel. Gran would bring her big beach hat and the picnic basket; Milo would bring his red bucket and his gentle, careful hands. Below them, the tide tucked every friend into deep cool water for the afternoon. "The tide will go out again someday," Gran said, smiling. "And when it does, the rescue patrol will be ready."
